en: Heating an aerosol spray can increases gas pressure inside, which can cause the metal container to explode.
Boiling tap water for at least one minute kills harmful bacteria and makes it safe to drink.
Mixing bleach with vinegar creates toxic chlorine gas, so you must never combine these two household cleaners.
Melting butter in a pan is a physical change because the liquid butter can solidify again when cooled.
Crushing and dissolving a time-release medicine pill in water can cause the body to absorb a dangerous overdose.
Rubber is an electrical insulator, which is why electricians wear rubber gloves to protect themselves from electric shocks.
Sweating cools your body because the liquid water absorbs heat from your skin to evaporate into a gas.
A foul smell from spoiled milk indicates a chemical change where bacteria produce harmful, toxic gases.
Oil floats on water during a kitchen grease fire, so you must never use water to extinguish it.
Sugar dissolves faster in hot tea than in iced tea because higher temperatures increase the solvent's kinetic energy.
Mixing baking soda and vinegar produces carbon dioxide gas, which can burst a tightly sealed glass bottle.
Solid dry ice sublimates directly into carbon dioxide gas, which can displace oxygen and cause suffocation indoors.
